entries.answer: DNA is the molecule that stores hereditary information in almost all living things. It is a double helix of four bases - A, T, C and G - and the order of those bases is the instruction set. A gene is a stretch of DNA that codes for a protein, and those proteins do nearly everything a cell does. You inherit half from each parent.

langs.tagalog: Ang DNA ay ang molekulang nag-iimbak ng impormasyong minana sa halos lahat ng bagay na buhay. Ang anyo nito ay isang baligtad na hagdan: dalawang mahabang hibla na magkatikom, may paires ng base na kemikal - karaniwang isinusulat bilang A, T, C at G - na nagsasama bilang hagdan. Ang pagkakasunod ng mga base ang siyang code, at ang pagbabasa nito ay sinasabi sa cell kung ano ang gagawin at kailan. Nagbibigay ang bawat magulang ng half, kaya katulad ng magulang ang mga anak ngunit hindi sila kopya ninuman sa kanila. Ang RNA ang kaugnay na molekulang talagang bumabasa ng code na iyon at gumagawa ng bagay rito. Halos lahat nito ay pareho sa halaman, hayop at bakteriya, kaya karaniwang gumagana sa yeast cell ang bahagi ng DNA ng tao, at kaya matutukoy ng ebidensya ng DNA ang isang tao mula sa buhok.
langs.bisaya: Ang DNA mao ang molecule nga nag-store sa hereditary info sa tanan nga living nga butang. Ang iyang anyo mao ang twirly nga hagdan: duha ka long nga strand nga maghagkot, naa nga pairs nga chemical nga base - kasagaran gisulat nga A, T, C ug G - nga naghugot nga sama sa mga rung. Ang order sa mga base na iya ang code, ug pagbasa niini maka-sabi sa cell unsang gayahon nga imong himoon ug kanus-a. Kaayo og katugtang matud ang parents nga katugtang anak nga dili man naa gayud nga kopya. Ang RNA mao ang related nga molecule nga gyud nga mabasa sa code ug himoon ang mga butas gikan niini. Kayo gyud nga pareho niini sa mga tanom, hayop ug bacteria, kana man kay kasagaran maa gyud nga human DNA ang moduha sa yeast cell, ug kana man nga DNA evidence makadawat og usa ka tawo gikan sa buhok.

entries.answer: Photosynthesis is how plants turn light into chemical energy, using carbon dioxide and water to make glucose and release oxygen. It happens in the chloroplast, and the light reactions split water to supply electrons and energy while a separate cycle fixes carbon. The reason it matters is not the sugar, which is only an intermediate, but that it is the origin of almost all organic carbon in the biosphere and of the oxygen in the atmosphere.

entries.answer: Evolution is change in the inherited characteristics of a population over generations, driven by heritable variation filtered by selection. It does not have a purpose, and that is the part people most often get wrong, because nothing in the mechanism is aiming at anything. It acts on existing variation rather than creating what is needed, which is why pressures in our environment produce no new adaptations in our own lifetime.

entries.answer: A cell is the smallest unit of life, and it is either prokaryotic with no nucleus or eukaryotic with one and other membrane-bound organelles. The nucleus protects the DNA and lets regulated copies be made, which is the innovation that allowed complex cells and eventually multicellular life. Mitochondria are separate organisms that were absorbed rather than invented, and they still carry their own small genome.

entries.answer: Genetic means relating to the information passed from parents to offspring, and the word is used for two different things that a learner often runs together: a genetic trait is a characteristic, while a genetic condition is an illness arising from a change in that information. The information itself is written in the DNA, in a sequence of four chemical letters, and instructions for building every part of an organism are laid out along it like an extremely long line of text. What makes it remarkable is how much of the variation in living things comes from changes in single letters rather than from whole genes, and how many such changes are harmless. This is why a family resemblance is a matter of probability rather than of copying: a child inherits one set from each parent, and the visible outcome is a mix influenced by many separate instructions. The practical consequence is that inherited conditions run in families in a recognisable pattern, and genetic counselling exists to estimate that probability before someone has children. It also explains why a trait can skip a generation, since a carrier may show nothing and still pass it on.
